idiom_name: os.File / net.Conn / bufio.Reader over the syscall package
implementation_notes: Go's standard library is the wrapper facade for OS and network APIs: os.File wraps a file descriptor and its methods proxy the file system calls, net.Conn/TCPConn wrap sockets, and the syscall package documents itself as the low-level layer those packages wrap, with File.SyscallConn (added in Go 1.12) as the typed escape hatch to the raw descriptor. For a resource the standard library does not cover, the same shape is written by hand: a small struct that owns the handle plus methods that forward to the C calls, kept minimal because Go callers accept interfaces rather than class hierarchies.
pitfalls: Go has no destructors: the facade must expose one obvious Close (or a scoped callback) and document that the value must not be used afterwards, because defer is the only teardown discipline available.
The syscall package is frozen in favour of golang.org/x/sys, so raw syscall use means carrying build tags and missing coverage for newer calls.
A struct holding a handle must not be copied by value: two copies mean two apparent owners of one descriptor.

variants.name: cgo binding for a C library the standard library does not cover
variants.idiom_name: import "C" plus a Go struct owning the C handle
variants.implementation_notes: When the non-OO API is a third-party C library, the facade is a cgo package: a Go struct stores the C handle, the methods call the imported functions, and a Go error is constructed from errno or the library's return code at the boundary. Go values passed into C must obey the cgo pointer rules, so strings cross as C.CString with an explicit C.free, and buffers cross as pointers to Go memory that the C side must not retain.
pitfalls: cgo calls are not free: each one crosses the runtime boundary, so a facade must expose batched operations instead of a method per raw call in hot paths.
Go pointers must not be stored on the C side, and C strings must be freed with C.free - a wrapper that keeps a C.CString to avoid re-allocating leaks it.
cgo changes the build: cross-compilation and static binaries need a C toolchain, so the binding should stay in a clearly separated package.
